Alice.summary: To understand human development, we must start from human nature, because biological characteristics explain intergroup differences and genetics explain individual IQ differences.

Bob.summary: Humans can be shaped differently depending on culture or social environment, because humans are homogeneous and intergroup differences in IQ are negligible.

c1.text: In order to understand human development, we must start from human nature.

c2.text: There are clear differences between groups, and biological characteristics play a decisive role in explaining intergroup differences.

c3.text: Differences in intelligence quotient between individuals are due to genetic factors.

c4.text: Intelligence quotients among groups divided by race, gender, etc. show almost no difference.

c6.text: Insisting on intergroup differences based on biological criteria stems from a motivation to uphold unequal social hierarchies.

c7.text: Social hierarchy only limits human variability.

c8.text: Humans can be shaped differently depending on culture or social environment.

h1.text: In every society throughout history, crime rates have been overwhelmingly higher in a particular group—males between the ages of 15 and 25.

h2.text: Regardless of culture or social environment, biological characteristics such as sex and age decisively influence human behavior and development.

h3.text: Various social reforms aimed at fairly developing the abilities of all members of society have failed.

h4.text: Social reforms are attempts to promote human development by changing culture or social environment.

h5.text: Changing culture or social environment does not shape human development or abilities.

h6.text: As a result of improving English education programs, the English test scores of most elementary school students increased significantly compared to before the improvement.

h7.text: Improving English education programs is a change in culture or social environment.

a.note: Consistent male youth crime rates across all societies support biological influence over culture, strengthening Alice rather than weakening her.

b.note: The failure of social reforms to develop abilities contradicts or attacks Bob's claim that environment shapes human development, so it does not strengthen Bob.

c.note: Significant score improvements through educational program changes demonstrate human development via environmental intervention, which strengthens Bob and weakens Alice, making both conjuncts false.
